chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When the news of a man's good state reaches you, then look at the goodness of his intellect, for truly he will be recompensed according to his intellect.'

key_terms.حُسْنُ حَالٍ: Good state/condition — the outward appearance of piety, prosperity, or righteousness
key_terms.حُسْنُ عَقْلٍ: Goodness of intellect — soundness and maturity of the rational-moral faculty
key_terms.يُجَازَى بِعَقْلِهِ: He will be recompensed by his intellect — divine recompense is proportional to one's intellectual capacity

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about judging a man's good condition and the role of intellect in divine recompense?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (saww) instructs his community to evaluate a person's good condition by examining the quality of their intellect, since divine recompense is proportional to one's rational faculty. This hadith, narrated through Imam al-Sadiq (AS) via al-Sakuni — a narrator acceptable to both Shia and Sunni traditions — underscores the Shia theological emphasis on 'aql (intellect) as the primary criterion of human worth and accountability. The original audience would have understood 'aql not merely as intelligence, but as the moral-rational faculty that distinguishes right from wrong.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘When (news) of the good state of a man reaches you, so look at the goodness of his intellect, for rather he would be Recompensed by (based upon the level of) his intellect’.
